scope: static trace of the node #115 EVM JSON bytes writer and its existing hex formatter

observations.fact: the existing send_to_evm_data JSON entry calls 0x25ce7e0 with its data pointer, length, and serializer
the writer calls 0x2a315b0 to create a temporary formatted String from the input byte slice
the writer appends an opening quote to the serializer Vec, passes the temporary String pointer and length to JSON escape helper 0x25bf330, and appends a closing quote
when the serializer Vec has no spare byte, the writer calls reserve with additional=1, alignment=1, element_size=1, then retries the quote append
the unwind cleanup checks temporary String capacity and calls the relocated deallocator when nonzero
the helper allocates a buffer of 2*input_length+2 bytes and writes the two-byte prefix 0x
a configuration bit at mask 0x200 selects a vectorized helper; the other path uses a scalar nibble loop
the scalar path maps both nibbles of each input byte through the digit table at 0x455d40
the vectorized path loads the same digit table at 0x455d40 before nibble lookup
the formatter configuration GOT slot is a symbol-free relative relocation to 0x6500098

inference: For successful formatting, the helper produces 0x followed by two lowercase hexadecimal digits per input byte; the empty slice therefore formats as 0x. Both scalar and vectorized paths use the same lowercase digit table.

The byte writer surrounds that formatted ASCII string with JSON quotes and passes it through the shared string escaper. Because its output alphabet contains no JSON-escapable byte, successful output is the quoted 0x-prefixed lowercase hex string.

The generic writer result and successful-allocation assumptions are limited to this observed static path; this packet does not establish all error, allocation-failure, or dynamic configuration behavior.
unresolved: source-level identity and intended meaning of configuration bit 0x200
the complete allocator failure and serialization Result/error contract
runtime use of the global configuration and behavior under live node conditions
limitations: The node artifact was read statically and was not executed or emulated.
The existing 0x25bf330 escape helper is reused by reference; its behavior was separately covered by evm-send-to-evm-data-json-115.
FDE extents are unwind ranges, not proof of source-level function boundaries.
